news.title: Brazil great Formiga says 2027 World Cup will ‘change players’ lives’
news.lede: SAO PAULO: Brazil legend Formiga believes next year’s Women’s World Cup in the country will be “an opportunity to change the lives of countless” players in South America. Former midfielder Formiga scored 29 goals in over 200 appearances for the Selecao before retiring aged 43 in 2021. The 2027 tournament will mark the first time the World Cup has been held in Latin America, in a country where women were banned from playing football as recently as 1979. “We have a tremendous opportunity to change the landscape of South American football,” Formiga told AFP at the “Esporte Cria” event organised by the Brazilian Olympic Committee in Sao Paulo.

news.title: UEFA and STRAUSS partner to elevate refereeing across European football
news.lede: The German company will support European football’s governing body in referee development, increasing visibility for match officials and bringing fans closer to the people behind the whistle. UEFA and STRAUSS, a leading brand for workwear, safety equipment and work-wearables, today announced a new partnership dedicated to supporting and developing refereeing across European football, reinforcing the vital role match officials play at every level of the game. Under the agreement, STRAUSS will become the first-ever official partner of UEFA refereeing, with its brand integrated across a range of refereeing activities and competitions.

news.title: The best do not always win the World Cup: Cafu | Football News
news.lede: Mumbai: On a stage at a college atrium, Cafu soaked in the adulation. Students, brandishing any Brazilian jersey they could find – from the present selection with ‘Neymar Jr’ printed on the back to quite a few with ‘Ronaldo’ – cheered him on. Cafu beckoned a few to toss their shirts forward for him to sign and send back.And then his eye caught a replica World Cup trophy. More silver than gold, it was handed over to him to pose with.

news.title: Cafu On India-Brazil Match And Football's Future
news.lede: Legendary Brazilian footballer Cafu shares insights on India's football development, Brazil's World Cup aspirations, and the evolving dynamics of the sport ahead of India's historic friendly against the five-time champions. Former Brazil captain Cafu on Friday said the Indian team will learn a lot from its first-ever international match against his country in Kolkata next month, though he admitted to the significant gap in the rankings between the two countries. India will face five-time World Cup champions Brazil in an international friendly at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata on October 3. "We hope that Brazil and India can play a great game.

news.title: FIFA, UEFA clash again over failed World Cup investment plan
news.lede: FIFA and UEFA are locked in a fresh row over the world governing body’s abandoned plan to sell stakes in the commercial rights to the World Cup to private investors. The latest dispute erupted after UEFA asked U.S. courts to compel FIFA and its partners to disclose documents related to the proposed investment structure, prompting FIFA to accuse the European governing body of pursuing a “smear campaign” and a “fishing expedition.” The confrontation represents a new escalation in the increasingly strained relationship between the two most powerful governing bodies in world football.
